text: Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. For a goods-not-received dispute the merchant must provide proof of delivery to the address the cardholder supplied, showing the carrier, the tracking number and the date the parcel was delivered. The acquirer submits the carrier's own record within 30 calendar days of the chargeback. A courier receipt without a photograph is accepted for any amount.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. For a goods-not-received dispute the merchant must provide proof of delivery to the address the cardholder supplied, showing the carrier, the tracking number and the date the parcel was delivered. The acquirer submits the carrier's own record within 30 calendar days of the chargeback. Above 250 dollars a delivery photograph or signature is mandatory.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. For a goods-not-received dispute the merchant must provide proof of delivery to the address the cardholder supplied, showing the carrier, the tracking number and the date the parcel was delivered. The response must reach the issuer within 20 business days and include the full shipping manifest. A courier receipt without a photograph is accepted for any amount.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. For a goods-not-received dispute the merchant must provide proof of delivery to the address the cardholder supplied, showing the carrier, the tracking number and the date the parcel was delivered. The response must reach the issuer within 20 business days and include the full shipping manifest. Above 250 dollars a delivery photograph or signature is mandatory.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. When goods were shipped to an address other than the one the cardholder gave, the merchant cannot rely on proof of delivery and the claim is generally upheld for the cardholder. The issuer may add a cardholder letter naming the correct address. Billing and shipping postcodes must both be listed.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. When goods were shipped to an address other than the one the cardholder gave, the merchant cannot rely on proof of delivery and the claim is generally upheld for the cardholder. The issuer may add a cardholder letter naming the correct address. Geolocation of the delivery scan may replace the postcode comparison.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. When goods were shipped to an address other than the one the cardholder gave, the merchant cannot rely on proof of delivery and the claim is generally upheld for the cardholder. A redirected shipment counts only if the cardholder requested the change in writing. Billing and shipping postcodes must both be listed.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. When goods were shipped to an address other than the one the cardholder gave, the merchant cannot rely on proof of delivery and the claim is generally upheld for the cardholder. A redirected shipment counts only if the cardholder requested the change in writing. Geolocation of the delivery scan may replace the postcode comparison.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. For digital goods or services not provided, the merchant shows that the download, login or access was completed by the cardholder's account after the purchase. Server logs must carry the account identifier and a timestamp. One successful login is sufficient.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. For digital goods or services not provided, the merchant shows that the download, login or access was completed by the cardholder's account after the purchase. Server logs must carry the account identifier and a timestamp. Two separate sessions of use are required after the purchase date.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. For digital goods or services not provided, the merchant shows that the download, login or access was completed by the cardholder's account after the purchase. Device fingerprint records are accepted alongside the IP address history. One successful login is sufficient.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. For digital goods or services not provided, the merchant shows that the download, login or access was completed by the cardholder's account after the purchase. Device fingerprint records are accepted alongside the IP address history. Two separate sessions of use are required after the purchase date.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. A cardholder must wait until the expected delivery date has passed before disputing non-receipt, unless the merchant has confirmed that the goods will not be sent. If no date was given the cardholder waits 15 calendar days from the transaction. The waiting period applies to services as well as goods.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. A cardholder must wait until the expected delivery date has passed before disputing non-receipt, unless the merchant has confirmed that the goods will not be sent. If no date was given the cardholder waits 15 calendar days from the transaction. The waiting period no longer applies to cancelled services.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. A cardholder must wait until the expected delivery date has passed before disputing non-receipt, unless the merchant has confirmed that the goods will not be sent. If no date was given the cardholder waits 30 days from the purchase. The waiting period applies to services as well as goods.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. A cardholder must wait until the expected delivery date has passed before disputing non-receipt, unless the merchant has confirmed that the goods will not be sent. If no date was given the cardholder waits 30 days from the purchase. The waiting period no longer applies to cancelled services.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. For merchandise not as described the cardholder must explain how the goods differed from the description at the time of purchase, and the merchant may respond with the listing and photographs. Expert opinion is optional for items under 500 dollars. The original advertisement must be supplied as a screenshot.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. For merchandise not as described the cardholder must explain how the goods differed from the description at the time of purchase, and the merchant may respond with the listing and photographs. Expert opinion is optional for items under 500 dollars. An archived copy of the product page with its date is acceptable.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. For merchandise not as described the cardholder must explain how the goods differed from the description at the time of purchase, and the merchant may respond with the listing and photographs. An independent appraisal is needed for jewellery and art. The original advertisement must be supplied as a screenshot.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. For merchandise not as described the cardholder must explain how the goods differed from the description at the time of purchase, and the merchant may respond with the listing and photographs. An independent appraisal is needed for jewellery and art. An archived copy of the product page with its date is acceptable.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. Before a not-as-described dispute the cardholder must attempt to return the merchandise, and proof of return shipment or the merchant's refusal of the return supports the claim. Return tracking must show delivery to the merchant's returns address. Returns are required for all items regardless of value.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. Before a not-as-described dispute the cardholder must attempt to return the merchandise, and proof of return shipment or the merchant's refusal of the return supports the claim. Return tracking must show delivery to the merchant's returns address. Items under 25 dollars are exempt from the return requirement.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. Before a not-as-described dispute the cardholder must attempt to return the merchandise, and proof of return shipment or the merchant's refusal of the return supports the claim. A postal receipt showing dispatch of the parcel back to the seller is enough. Returns are required for all items regardless of value.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. Before a not-as-described dispute the cardholder must attempt to return the merchandise, and proof of return shipment or the merchant's refusal of the return supports the claim. A postal receipt showing dispatch of the parcel back to the seller is enough. Items under 25 dollars are exempt from the return requirement.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. For counterfeit merchandise the cardholder provides a statement from the brand owner, a customs authority or a qualified expert that the goods are not genuine. The cardholder need not return counterfeit goods to the merchant. A cardholder's own statement may be accepted for items under 100 dollars.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. For counterfeit merchandise the cardholder provides a statement from the brand owner, a customs authority or a qualified expert that the goods are not genuine. The cardholder need not return counterfeit goods to the merchant. A third-party statement is required at every value.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. For counterfeit merchandise the cardholder provides a statement from the brand owner, a customs authority or a qualified expert that the goods are not genuine. Counterfeit goods must be destroyed or retained, never sent back. A cardholder's own statement may be accepted for items under 100 dollars.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. For counterfeit merchandise the cardholder provides a statement from the brand owner, a customs authority or a qualified expert that the goods are not genuine. Counterfeit goods must be destroyed or retained, never sent back. A third-party statement is required at every value.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. The cardholder must make a good-faith attempt to resolve a quality dispute with the merchant before the issuer raises it, and must describe that attempt. The attempt is described in the cardholder's own words with its date. Telephone contact alone satisfies the requirement.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. The cardholder must make a good-faith attempt to resolve a quality dispute with the merchant before the issuer raises it, and must describe that attempt. The attempt is described in the cardholder's own words with its date. Contact must be made through a channel that leaves a written record.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. The cardholder must make a good-faith attempt to resolve a quality dispute with the merchant before the issuer raises it, and must describe that attempt. Email or chat transcripts with the merchant are attached where they exist. Telephone contact alone satisfies the requirement.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. The cardholder must make a good-faith attempt to resolve a quality dispute with the merchant before the issuer raises it, and must describe that attempt. Email or chat transcripts with the merchant are attached where they exist. Contact must be made through a channel that leaves a written record.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. For a cancelled recurring transaction the cardholder shows that the subscription was cancelled before the charge, with the cancellation date and any confirmation number. A cancellation confirmation code from the merchant is the preferred evidence. Cancellation must have occurred at least 3 days before billing.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. For a cancelled recurring transaction the cardholder shows that the subscription was cancelled before the charge, with the cancellation date and any confirmation number. A cancellation confirmation code from the merchant is the preferred evidence. Cancellation any time before the billing date qualifies.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. For a cancelled recurring transaction the cardholder shows that the subscription was cancelled before the charge, with the cancellation date and any confirmation number. The issuer may rely on the cardholder's dated account of the cancellation. Cancellation must have occurred at least 3 days before billing.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. For a cancelled recurring transaction the cardholder shows that the subscription was cancelled before the charge, with the cancellation date and any confirmation number. The issuer may rely on the cardholder's dated account of the cancellation. Cancellation any time before the billing date qualifies.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. A merchant defending a recurring charge must show that its cancellation terms were clearly disclosed and accepted by the cardholder at sign-up. A checkbox record with a timestamp is required. Terms in the general conditions are acceptable.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. A merchant defending a recurring charge must show that its cancellation terms were clearly disclosed and accepted by the cardholder at sign-up. A checkbox record with a timestamp is required. Terms must be shown separately from the general conditions.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. A merchant defending a recurring charge must show that its cancellation terms were clearly disclosed and accepted by the cardholder at sign-up. The terms must appear on the same screen as the payment button. Terms in the general conditions are acceptable.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. A merchant defending a recurring charge must show that its cancellation terms were clearly disclosed and accepted by the cardholder at sign-up. The terms must appear on the same screen as the payment button. Terms must be shown separately from the general conditions.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. When a free trial converts to a paid subscription, the merchant must have told the cardholder the price, the conversion date and how to cancel before the first charge. A reminder must be sent 7 days before the first charge. The reminder may be sent by email only.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. When a free trial converts to a paid subscription, the merchant must have told the cardholder the price, the conversion date and how to cancel before the first charge. A reminder must be sent 7 days before the first charge. The reminder must be sent through the channel used at enrolment.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. When a free trial converts to a paid subscription, the merchant must have told the cardholder the price, the conversion date and how to cancel before the first charge. A reminder must be sent at least 3 days before conversion. The reminder may be sent by email only.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. When a free trial converts to a paid subscription, the merchant must have told the cardholder the price, the conversion date and how to cancel before the first charge. A reminder must be sent at least 3 days before conversion. The reminder must be sent through the channel used at enrolment.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. For annual renewals the merchant must notify the cardholder of the upcoming renewal and its amount, and a dispute succeeds if no notice was sent. Notice is due between 30 and 60 days before renewal. Notice is required only for amounts above 50 dollars.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. For annual renewals the merchant must notify the cardholder of the upcoming renewal and its amount, and a dispute succeeds if no notice was sent. Notice is due between 30 and 60 days before renewal. Notice is required for every renewal amount.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. For annual renewals the merchant must notify the cardholder of the upcoming renewal and its amount, and a dispute succeeds if no notice was sent. Notice is due at least 14 days before renewal. Notice is required only for amounts above 50 dollars.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. For annual renewals the merchant must notify the cardholder of the upcoming renewal and its amount, and a dispute succeeds if no notice was sent. Notice is due at least 14 days before renewal. Notice is required for every renewal amount.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. For credit not processed the cardholder provides the credit voucher, refund acknowledgment or return receipt showing that the merchant agreed to refund. An undated voucher is accepted if the transaction reference appears on it. A verbal promise of refund recorded by the issuer is sufficient.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. For credit not processed the cardholder provides the credit voucher, refund acknowledgment or return receipt showing that the merchant agreed to refund. An undated voucher is accepted if the transaction reference appears on it. A verbal promise must be confirmed in writing by the merchant.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. For credit not processed the cardholder provides the credit voucher, refund acknowledgment or return receipt showing that the merchant agreed to refund. The voucher must be dated and show the amount of the credit. A verbal promise of refund recorded by the issuer is sufficient.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. For credit not processed the cardholder provides the credit voucher, refund acknowledgment or return receipt showing that the merchant agreed to refund. The voucher must be dated and show the amount of the credit. A verbal promise must be confirmed in writing by the merchant.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. A merchant may defend a refund claim by showing a disclosed no-refund or store-credit policy that the cardholder accepted at purchase. The policy must be printed on the receipt. Policies posted at the till are accepted.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. A merchant may defend a refund claim by showing a disclosed no-refund or store-credit policy that the cardholder accepted at purchase. The policy must be printed on the receipt. Policies must be acknowledged by the cardholder.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. A merchant may defend a refund claim by showing a disclosed no-refund or store-credit policy that the cardholder accepted at purchase. The policy must be shown before the cardholder pays. Policies posted at the till are accepted.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. A merchant may defend a refund claim by showing a disclosed no-refund or store-credit policy that the cardholder accepted at purchase. The policy must be shown before the cardholder pays. Policies must be acknowledged by the cardholder.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. The cardholder must allow the merchant time to process a promised credit before disputing, counted from the date on the credit voucher or the return. The waiting time is 15 calendar days. No waiting time applies if the voucher is undated.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. The cardholder must allow the merchant time to process a promised credit before disputing, counted from the date on the credit voucher or the return. The waiting time is 15 calendar days. An undated voucher starts the waiting time on the return date.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. The cardholder must allow the merchant time to process a promised credit before disputing, counted from the date on the credit voucher or the return. The waiting time is 10 business days. No waiting time applies if the voucher is undated.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. The cardholder must allow the merchant time to process a promised credit before disputing, counted from the date on the credit voucher or the return. The waiting time is 10 business days. An undated voucher starts the waiting time on the return date.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. Where a merchant issued only part of the promised credit, the dispute is limited to the unrefunded difference. Restocking fees disclosed at purchase are not disputable. The cardholder must state the partial amount received.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. Where a merchant issued only part of the promised credit, the dispute is limited to the unrefunded difference. Restocking fees disclosed at purchase are not disputable. The issuer calculates the difference from clearing records.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. Where a merchant issued only part of the promised credit, the dispute is limited to the unrefunded difference. Restocking fees are disputable unless shown on the receipt. The cardholder must state the partial amount received.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. Where a merchant issued only part of the promised credit, the dispute is limited to the unrefunded difference. Restocking fees are disputable unless shown on the receipt. The issuer calculates the difference from clearing records.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. For duplicate processing the issuer shows two transactions with the same card, merchant, amount and date, and the merchant may answer with proof of two separate purchases. The two transactions must share the authorization code. Transactions within 7 days qualify.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. For duplicate processing the issuer shows two transactions with the same card, merchant, amount and date, and the merchant may answer with proof of two separate purchases. The two transactions must share the authorization code. Transactions within 15 days qualify.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. For duplicate processing the issuer shows two transactions with the same card, merchant, amount and date, and the merchant may answer with proof of two separate purchases. Matching acquirer reference numbers are strong evidence of duplication. Transactions within 7 days qualify.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. For duplicate processing the issuer shows two transactions with the same card, merchant, amount and date, and the merchant may answer with proof of two separate purchases. Matching acquirer reference numbers are strong evidence of duplication. Transactions within 15 days qualify.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. When a cardholder paid for the same goods by another method, the cardholder supplies proof of the other payment, such as a cash receipt or a bank transfer record. The other payment must be to the same merchant outlet. A bank statement line is sufficient proof.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. When a cardholder paid for the same goods by another method, the cardholder supplies proof of the other payment, such as a cash receipt or a bank transfer record. The other payment must be to the same merchant outlet. A receipt from the merchant is required for cash payments.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. When a cardholder paid for the same goods by another method, the cardholder supplies proof of the other payment, such as a cash receipt or a bank transfer record. Payment to any outlet of the same merchant is accepted. A bank statement line is sufficient proof.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. When a cardholder paid for the same goods by another method, the cardholder supplies proof of the other payment, such as a cash receipt or a bank transfer record. Payment to any outlet of the same merchant is accepted. A receipt from the merchant is required for cash payments.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. A merchant defending a duplicate claim provides itemized receipts or order records showing that each transaction was a separate purchase. Each receipt must show a distinct order number. Signed receipts are required for both transactions.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. A merchant defending a duplicate claim provides itemized receipts or order records showing that each transaction was a separate purchase. Each receipt must show a distinct order number. Unsigned electronic receipts are accepted.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. A merchant defending a duplicate claim provides itemized receipts or order records showing that each transaction was a separate purchase. Each receipt must show the time of sale to the minute. Signed receipts are required for both transactions.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. A merchant defending a duplicate claim provides itemized receipts or order records showing that each transaction was a separate purchase. Each receipt must show the time of sale to the minute. Unsigned electronic receipts are accepted.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. For card-absent fraud the merchant may submit compelling evidence that the same cardholder made earlier undisputed purchases using the same device or account. Two prior transactions between 120 and 365 days old are required. Matching shipping address alone links the transactions.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. For card-absent fraud the merchant may submit compelling evidence that the same cardholder made earlier undisputed purchases using the same device or account. Two prior transactions between 120 and 365 days old are required. At least two data elements must match, such as device and IP address.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. For card-absent fraud the merchant may submit compelling evidence that the same cardholder made earlier undisputed purchases using the same device or account. One prior transaction within 180 days is required. Matching shipping address alone links the transactions.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. For card-absent fraud the merchant may submit compelling evidence that the same cardholder made earlier undisputed purchases using the same device or account. One prior transaction within 180 days is required. At least two data elements must match, such as device and IP address.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. A merchant may show that address verification and the card security code matched at authorization when answering a card-absent fraud claim. A full AVS match must be shown in the authorization record. AVS alone was sufficient evidence.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. A merchant may show that address verification and the card security code matched at authorization when answering a card-absent fraud claim. A full AVS match must be shown in the authorization record. AVS results are supporting evidence only.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. A merchant may show that address verification and the card security code matched at authorization when answering a card-absent fraud claim. A partial AVS match is accepted with a CVV match. AVS alone was sufficient evidence.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. A merchant may show that address verification and the card security code matched at authorization when answering a card-absent fraud claim. A partial AVS match is accepted with a CVV match. AVS results are supporting evidence only.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. When a card-absent transaction was authenticated with 3-D Secure, fraud liability shifts to the issuer and the merchant cites the authentication value. The shift applies only to fully authenticated transactions. Version 1 authentication is accepted.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. When a card-absent transaction was authenticated with 3-D Secure, fraud liability shifts to the issuer and the merchant cites the authentication value. The shift applies only to fully authenticated transactions. Only version 2 authentication shifts liability.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. When a card-absent transaction was authenticated with 3-D Secure, fraud liability shifts to the issuer and the merchant cites the authentication value. Attempted authentication also shifts liability. Version 1 authentication is accepted.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. When a card-absent transaction was authenticated with 3-D Secure, fraud liability shifts to the issuer and the merchant cites the authentication value. Attempted authentication also shifts liability. Only version 2 authentication shifts liability.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2024.2. A merchant may rely on device identifiers, IP addresses and login history linking the disputed purchase to the cardholder's prior activity. The IP address must be shown with the geolocation. Email address match is sufficient.

Network A dispute rules, edition 2025.2. A merchant may rely on device identifiers, IP addresses and login history linking the disputed purchase to the cardholder's prior activity. The IP address must be shown with the geolocation. Email match must be combined with a device match.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2024.1. A merchant may rely on device identifiers, IP addresses and login history linking the disputed purchase to the cardholder's prior activity. The device identifier must persist across sessions. Email address match is sufficient.

Network B dispute rules, edition 2025.1. A merchant may rely on device identifiers, IP addresses and login history linking the disputed purchase to the cardholder's prior activity. The device identifier must persist across sessions. Email match must be combined with a device match.

Regulation E requires a financial institution to investigate an error reported on a debit card account within 10 business days, or within 45 days if it gives provisional credit, and to report the results to the consumer in writing.
Regulation Z requires a card issuer to acknowledge a billing error notice on a credit card within 30 days and to resolve it within two billing cycles and no more than 90 days.
Letters to cardholders state what the records show, never accuse the cardholder, explain the next steps and the cardholder's rights, and use plain language.
Messages to merchants include only the data the network requires for the dispute; never send the cardholder's contact details or information about other accounts.
Card numbers, email addresses and telephone numbers are redacted from narratives before they are placed in prompts or logs.
